name: Building intrusion detection inside the fence, multi-temporal

identity.method_name: Multi-temporal building-footprint point-in-polygon / footprint-overlap counting within a buffer ring (vector GIS intrusion counting), using GOOGLE/Research/open-buildings-temporal/v1, Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints, and OpenStreetMap historical extracts (ohsome/OSHDB)
identity.core_idea: For each lake, build the legal buffer ring (from item B1) around the boundary polygon (from item B2), then for each available year intersect a building-footprint vector layer against the ring using GeoPandas spatial join / shapely STRtree indexing, counting structures whose footprint overlaps the ring above a chosen threshold (or whose centroid falls inside it). Repeating this across years drawn from a genuinely multi-temporal footprint source turns a single frozen intrusion count into a year-by-year encroachment trend -- the concrete 'a structure is standing where the lake legally is' signal, distinct from and immune to the water-area confounds (desilting, hyacinth) that a pixel-based water/vegetation series suffers from.
identity.official_dataset_ids: GOOGLE/Research/open-buildings-temporal/v1 (Google Earth Engine catalog, annual layers 2016-2023 -- confirmed 8 annual layers, stopping one year short of this project's 2025 endpoint; ~4 m effective resolution delivered as 0.5 m raster bands: uncalibrated 0-1 building-presence confidence, fractional building count 0-0.0216/pixel, building height 0-100 m; derived from Sentinel-2 via Sirko et al. 2021, arXiv:2107.12283). Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints (github.com/microsoft/GlobalMLBuildingFootprints, per-country/quadkey GeoJSON, single rolling current snapshot, not officially archived by year). OpenStreetMap full-edit-history via the ohsome API / OSHDB (ohsome-py client), which can reconstruct a footprint snapshot as of any past timestamp back to the first edit in an area (commonly 2007+ for India). Current project baseline for comparison: single 2026 OSM snapshot, 420,080 footprints, zero temporal variance.

fit_to_project.ground_truth_proxy_strategy: Threshold rule, not a learned model: 'a building footprint (or overlap fraction above a threshold) falls inside the legal buffer ring in year Y' is used directly as the encroachment proxy, with no classifier and no manual encroachment-labelling step. The cost sits entirely in data acquisition, not labelling: an estimated 3-4 student-days to pull and cross-check Open Buildings Temporal (GEE), Microsoft Footprints, and an ohsome historical extract for the 6 lake AOIs, per this research.
fit_to_project.input_required: A vector building-footprint layer with genuine year-to-year variation for each of the 6 lake AOIs, plus the buffer-ring polygon(s) from B1/B2. The project currently has neither: only a single constant 2026 OSM snapshot (420,080 footprints) with no usable year field. Three acquisition routes exist, none already in hand: (a) GOOGLE/Research/open-buildings-temporal/v1 via Earth Engine, annual 2016-2023; (b) Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints, a single current snapshot only; (c) an ohsome/OSHDB historical query against OSM's full edit history, the only route that can reach further back than 2016.
fit_to_project.viable_with_42_rows: only-if-reframed. The geometric intersection itself operates per building footprint against ring geometry (tens of thousands of footprints per lake), a far larger effective n than 42; the resulting per-lake-per-year counts (or overlap areas) can then be folded back into the existing 42-row table as new columns (e.g. buildings_in_buffer_count, overlap_area_m2). It should not be reported or analysed as if the underlying geometry test itself had only 42 independent observations.
fit_to_project.viable_without_ground_truth: yes -- no labelled encroachment examples are needed; footprint-intersects-ring is a direct geometric proxy for the missing label, in the same threshold-rule spirit as the project's existing MNDWI/NDVI baseline.
fit_to_project.resolution_match_20m: No, and this is the load-bearing finding of the item: the intrusion-counting step must not be done on the 20 m Sentinel-2 raster grid. A ~30 m legal buffer ring is only about 1.5 pixels wide at 20 m resolution, so a single pixel can span the whole ring and margin on both sides, making raster-based point-in-polygon or overlap logic unable to distinguish a building 5 m inside the fence from one 25 m inside or just outside. Vector building-footprint data (Open Buildings, MS Footprints, OSM), which carries metre-scale precision independent of the Sentinel-2 grid, is therefore the only workable route for this step; the 20 m raster should remain confined to the water/vegetation classification, not be used for building intrusion.
fit_to_project.label_source_needed: none for the counting step itself -- geometric intersection against the buffer polygon substitutes for a label. (Open Buildings' own footprints are the output of a Google-trained CNN, but that supervision is external and pre-baked; the project only consumes the released output.)
fit_to_project.fixes_which_stated_limitation: Directly fixes limitation (2), OpenStreetMap is one snapshot so buildings cannot show growth: Open Buildings Temporal (annual 2016-2023) and an ohsome historical extract both introduce genuine year-to-year variance the current OSM-2026-snapshot pipeline lacks. Does not by itself fix (1) 42 rows, (3) no ground truth, or (4) dry-season-only imagery, though its output can be added as new columns to the existing 42-row table.
fit_to_project.handles_desilting_confound: Yes -- this is the item's central value. A drained-for-desilting lake (Bellandur: 15.7 ha (2019) -> 0.4 ha (2021) -> 107.9 ha (2025)) shows no change in a building-footprint-in-buffer count, because desilting drains water, it does not place or remove structures. A water-area time series alone cannot separate desilting from encroachment; a building-intrusion series run alongside it can, since only encroachment moves the building count.
fit_to_project.handles_hyacinth_confound: Not directly -- building-footprint counting is orthogonal to the water-vs-vegetation misclassification hyacinth mats cause (Bellandur 2019: 16 ha water, 260 ha vegetation of a 315 ha footprint; MDPI Remote Sensing 2020, doi 10.3390/rs12223843). It neither worsens nor resolves that confound; it supplies an independent cross-check signal that does not depend on the water/vegetation classifier at all.
fit_to_project.legal_traceability: More direct than pixel-based water/vegetation counting: a building whose footprint (or overlap fraction) falls inside the chosen buffer ring (B1's 30 m Master Plan/KTCDA figure, or the 75 m NGT figure as a bracketing case) is a structure standing inside a specific legally-defined protected zone -- the closest this project gets to an actual encroachment claim, as distinct from a lake merely being dry. The ring itself carries all of B1's legal caveats (no single binding number, must state distance and authority explicitly). The building-footprint layer carries no legal status of its own -- it is a geometric/imagery-derived product (Google/Microsoft/OSM), not a cadastral or Survey-of-India record -- so 'building inside the ring' is a strong indicator, not a title-record adjudication.
fit_to_project.temporal_granularity: Genuinely variable only if Open Buildings Temporal or an ohsome historical extract is used. Open Buildings Temporal is annual for 2016-2023 (one year short of the project's 2025 endpoint); ohsome can reconstruct a footprint snapshot for any past date back to OSM's first local edit (commonly 2007+ for India). Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints is NOT multi-temporal -- a single rolling current snapshot per country/quadkey with no official per-year archive -- so using it alone reproduces the project's existing zero-variance problem. [uncertain] Peri-urban Bengaluru lake buffers are the kind of area where OSM building coverage often arrives via bulk mapathon/import events rather than continuous organic editing; if most of the 420,080 current footprints came from one or a few import bursts, an ohsome time series could show a flat count then a step-jump at the import date rather than real construction growth. This could not be confirmed or denied for Bengaluru specifically without directly inspecting each AOI's OSM changeset history.

implementation.libraries: geopandas, shapely>=2.0 (STRtree), pyproj (EPSG:32643), earthengine-api / geemap (for GOOGLE/Research/open-buildings-temporal/v1), ohsome (ohsome-py, HeiGIT-hosted API, free research signup key), requests (direct Microsoft Footprints GeoJSON download).
implementation.pretrained_weights: Not applicable to the counting step itself (pure geometry). The upstream Open Buildings Temporal layer is produced by a pretrained Google CNN (Sirko et al. 2021, arXiv:2107.12283) trained on Sentinel-2 plus high-resolution reference imagery across the Global South; the project only consumes the released Earth Engine output and does not load or fine-tune those weights.
implementation.licence: GOOGLE/Research/open-buildings-temporal/v1: dual CC-BY 4.0 and ODbL 1.0. Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints: ODbL. OpenStreetMap / ohsome: ODbL; ohsome API is free for research use with a signup key. None block academic use; ODbL requires share-alike attribution if the derived building-count layer itself is redistributed.
implementation.compute_requirement: CPU-only feasible. STRtree-indexed intersection of hundreds of thousands of footprints against 6 lakes' ring polygons is a sub-minute laptop operation. The Earth Engine pull for Open Buildings Temporal runs server-side within free EE quota for 6 small AOIs; ohsome API calls are free-tier and lightweight for 6 AOIs x a handful of timestamps. No GPU or Colab/Kaggle allocation is needed for this item.
implementation.student_days: 3-4 student-days to pull and cross-check all three sources (Open Buildings Temporal via GEE, MS Footprints, and an ohsome historical extract) and run overlap-fraction counting per ring per year; 1.5-2 days if scoped to a single source, with the caveat that ohsome-only risks the import-step-function artifact and Open-Buildings-only stops at 2023 and carries the near-water suppression risk noted under risk.failure_modes.

evaluation.metrics: No single accuracy metric applies since there is no ground truth. The intended output is a per-lake time series of (a) building count inside the ring and (b) total footprint-overlap area inside the ring, reported alongside a sensitivity band across at least two counting rules (any-intersection vs overlap-fraction >50%) and at least two buffer distances (30 m, 75 m, per B1). A meaningful internal check is whether the count changes in step with the underlying data source's own update cadence (annual Open Buildings layers, or specific ohsome query dates) rather than showing random noise.
evaluation.validation_protocol: Not a trained model, so no train/test split applies. The correct protocol is a disclosed sensitivity sweep fixed before results are inspected: report intrusion counts under both the any-intersection and overlap-fraction-threshold rules, and under both the 30 m and 75 m buffer candidates, for every lake-year, rather than reporting only whichever combination produces the most dramatic trend.
evaluation.leakage_risk: Not classic train/test leakage but (a) researcher-degrees-of-freedom in choosing which counting rule and buffer width to report -- must be pre-disclosed as a sensitivity band, mirroring B1; and (b) mistaking an OSM bulk-import step-jump for genuine multi-year construction growth, which would fabricate a false encroachment trend from a mapping artifact -- this must be checked against each AOI's actual OSM changeset history before the series is trusted.
evaluation.uncertainty_reporting: No calibrated interval is native to the geometric counting method. The honest uncertainty treatment is the counting-rule and buffer-distance sensitivity band described above (min/max intrusion count across the two rules and two buffer widths), plus an explicit caveat that Open Buildings' 'building presence' band is documented as an uncalibrated 0-1 confidence score, not a true probability, and should not be thresholded and reported as if it carried a formal false-positive rate.
evaluation.augmentation_honesty_risk: not applicable -- no synthetic data generation or augmentation is involved in vector footprint counting.

evidence.published_performance: No accuracy metric applies to the counting step itself, since it is a deterministic geometry operation, not a model. For the upstream Open Buildings 2.5D Temporal detection pipeline, a third-party benchmark (arXiv:2511.12104, 'TEMPO') reports precision 0.77, recall 0.93, F1 0.84 on a Global South subset [verify -- third-party benchmark, not Google's own validation, and not evaluated on this project's own 6 lakes]. Google's own documentation describes the 'building presence' band only as an uncalibrated 0-1 confidence score, explicitly not a probability.
evidence.study_area_of_that_work: Open Buildings Temporal / TEMPO benchmark: Global South-wide (58M km^2 footprint spanning Africa, South Asia including India, SE Asia, Latin America, Caribbean), not Bengaluru-specific or lake-specific. Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints: global, country-by-country, India among the largest-coverage countries by footprint count, again not lake-specific. No published study was found applying any of these three sources specifically to Indian lake or wetland encroachment -- a genuine literature gap, not a search failure.
evidence.applies_to_indian_urban_lakes: No dedicated Bengaluru-lake or Indian-wetland-encroachment application was found for any of the three sources. The only Bengaluru-specific application found used the static (non-temporal) Open Buildings v3 polygon product for general building-density mapping, unrelated to lakes or encroachment (https://www.agsrt.com/building-density-analysis-bengaluru). Closest indirect analogue: an informal-settlement building-dataset quality comparison across 5 Global South cities (arXiv:2508.12872), which does not include Bengaluru or lake buffers.
evidence.evidence_recency: 2025-2026 for the strongest supporting material: Google Research's Open Buildings 2.5D Temporal dataset documentation and blog announcement, and a companion Nature Scientific Data quality paper (2025, doi via nature.com/articles/s41597-025-06132-z); TEMPO benchmark, arXiv:2511.12104 (2025) [verify]. Foundational methodology paper (Sirko et al., arXiv:2107.12283) is from 2021. ohsome/OSHDB documentation is continuously maintained (2024-2026 current). Nothing load-bearing here is pre-2020.
evidence.primary_sources: GOOGLE/Research/open-buildings-temporal/v1 catalog page: https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/GOOGLE_Research_open-buildings-temporal_v1 ; Google Research announcement: https://research.google/blog/open-buildings-25d-temporal-dataset-tracks-building-changes-across-the-global-south/ ; project site: https://sites.research.google/gr/open-buildings/temporal/ ; methodology paper, Sirko et al. 2021: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.12283 ; water-body/dilation filtering discussion: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.04106 and https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-025-06132-z and https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.GIScience.2023.35 ; TEMPO benchmark [verify]: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.12104 ; Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints: https://github.com/microsoft/GlobalMLBuildingFootprints ; ohsome API docs: https://docs.ohsome.org/ohsome-api/v1/ and https://ohsome.org ; ohsome-py client: https://github.com/GIScience/ohsome-py and https://pypi.org/project/ohsome/ ; shapely STRtree docs: https://shapely.readthedocs.io/en/stable/strtree.html ; existing Bengaluru Open Buildings application (static, non-temporal): https://www.agsrt.com/building-density-analysis-bengaluru ; informal-settlement dataset comparison: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.12872 ; hyacinth cross-check reference already used elsewhere in this project: MDPI Remote Sensing 2020, doi 10.3390/rs12223843.

risk.failure_modes: (1) [uncertain] The most important risk found: Google's Open Buildings detection pipeline filters candidate polygons using a WorldCover land-cover mask dilated by 250 m, and separately documents removing 'all buildings found in water bodies, as mapped in OpenStreetMap ... including stilt houses and boathouses' (per methodology summaries in arXiv:2506.04106 and Nature Scientific Data 2025). A 250 m suppression buffer is roughly 8x the project's ~30 m legal buffer, meaning structures built 0-75 m from a lake edge -- precisely what this item targets -- sit in the exact zone the dataset's own QA is tuned to treat as likely false positives and discard, risking systematic under-counting of real near-lake encroachment in the dataset's own favoured direction. This is inferred from secondary methodology summaries, not verified by testing on the project's own 6 lakes. (2) Treating Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints as multi-temporal reproduces the project's existing zero-variance problem, since it is itself a single rolling current snapshot. (3) An ohsome-derived series can mistake an OSM bulk-import/mapathon event for real multi-year construction growth (flat count then step-jump at the import date), which must be checked against each AOI's OSM changeset history before being trusted. (4) Centroid-in-polygon counting at a ring only ~1-2 building-widths wide has a roughly coin-flip edge bias for footprints straddling the boundary, which can swing the headline count substantially depending on the rule chosen -- must be disclosed as a sensitivity band, not hidden behind one number.
risk.panel_defensibility: A panel will ask 'why trust a building count that Google's own pipeline may have already filtered out near water?' and 'how do you know a jump in your OSM-based count is real construction and not a mapping import?' This item survives those questions only if both caveats are stated up front as named limitations of the specific sources chosen, not papered over. It survives the standard 'no ground truth' question better than a pixel-based water/vegetation method does, because a building footprint standing inside a legally-defined ring is a more direct and legible encroachment claim than a change in reflectance-derived land-cover class -- but only if the buffer-distance ambiguity (B1) and the counting-rule ambiguity above are both disclosed.
risk.honest_expectation: Realistically achievable: a per-lake-per-year building-intrusion count and overlap-area series for 2016-2023 from Open Buildings Temporal (one year short of the project's 2025 endpoint), cross-checked qualitatively against an ohsome historical extract after manual changeset-history inspection, reported as a bracketed range (any-intersection vs overlap>50%, 30 m vs 75 m buffer) rather than a single number. Given the near-water suppression bias in Open Buildings, near-zero or slow, small rises are plausible even for genuinely encroached lakes, and a null or muted result for some lakes is an acceptable, reportable outcome. This will not deliver a fully validated, ground-truthed encroachment count, and does not extend past 2023 without the ohsome route, whose own reliability for Bengaluru specifically is itself unconfirmed.

verdict.recommended_rank: adopt-if-time -- the single most legally-legible, desilting-immune encroachment signal available to the project, but it needs 3-4 student-days across three data sources with non-trivial per-source caveats (near-water suppression bias in Open Buildings, non-temporal nature of MS Footprints, import-artifact risk in ohsome) that must each be disclosed rather than silently trusted.
verdict.one_line_for_the_guide: Building footprints (Google Open Buildings Temporal 2016-2023, cross-checked against an OSM historical extract) can be counted inside the legal buffer ring year by year to give a direct, desilting-immune encroachment signal that a water-area time series cannot provide, but only vector footprint data -- never the 20 m Sentinel-2 raster grid, which is too coarse for a ~30 m-wide ring -- can do this, and both the counting rule and the buffer distance must be reported as a sensitivity range rather than one headline number.
